multi_visual_scene_design_v2.exact_print_copy: Across the Mountain Lake bridge, Wilson Look planted four hooves and raised his axe. “The Belt Keeper comes to ask permission?” he called. From the far landing, Austin Byars lifted his hooded head, red eyes burning in shadow. “Not yours,” came the answer. Behind Wilson, the carter held his horse and wagon still. Wilson made a mocking path between them. “After you, Austin.” The old lantern swung, the storm tore at their cloaks, and both warriors lowered their weapons. Neither intended to surrender the crossing. They charged.
multi_visual_scene_design_v2.transition_out: Both closing on the reset center stone; sword and axe raised; lantern still at midpoint; no strike or slip yet.

multi_visual_scene_design_v2.exact_print_copy: Their first collision rang against the lantern stones. Wilson drove his axe down; Austin caught its haft with his sword and turned aside instead of meeting the centaur’s weight head-on. Hooves hammered the narrow deck. Wilson twisted for a second cut, forcing Austin toward the parapet. “He was here before us,” Austin said, glancing at the waiting carter. He slipped inside the next swing and struck Wilson’s armored upper body. The impact shoved the huge warrior backward. His hind hooves crossed on rain-slick stone. All four feet fought for purchase as the parapet rushed toward him.
multi_visual_scene_design_v2.transition_out: Wilson is at edge with weight moving outward, all 4 hooves visible, still not in water; Austin sword held, Belt remains with Austin, bridge intact.

multi_visual_scene_design_v2.exact_print_copy: Austin’s final blow carried through the clash. Four hooves scraped for grip; Wilson’s enormous armored body pitched over the intact parapet and vanished into the raging, storm-churned water. The carter stopped breathing. Even Austin stepped to the edge, his gold belt still fixed at his waist. Waves battered the pier. Then Wilson’s dark head broke the foam—coughing, alive. Only when the great centaur reached toward shore did Austin release the small jester’s cap. “My jester,” he said, almost without triumph. His Majesty’s Blood 168.20 · D0nkey K0ng 129.75.
multi_visual_scene_design_v2.transition_out: Wilson alive, injured only if separately sourced (do not infer), the cart can cross later; Austin retains championship belt; cap may appear only after Wilson surfaces; no World permanence inferred.
